historical_growth.basis_note: The FY2024->FY2025 boundary is a continuing-operations restatement (Detection and Interconnect removed), so any CAGR spanning it measures the divestiture, not the business. The 3- and 5-year figures below are TOTAL-GROUP, PRE-DIVESTITURE (FY2019->FY2024 for 5yr, FY2021->FY2024 for 3yr) and serve as margin/cyclicality context only. The only clean continuing-basis data point is FY2025->FY2026: revenue +2.1% reported (+1.2% organic, +M&A, -FX), HOP +2.8%.
historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest income), total group: FY2019 202, FY2021 396 (COVID working-capital release, unrepeatable peak), FY2024 293. The 3yr figure is from that FY2021 peak and is not informative; the 5yr figure is the cleaner read.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 organic revenue growth guidance (~4%, 22 Sep 2026), used as the near-term anchor; the medium-term 5-7% organic target is treated as the bull axis, not the base, because FY2026 delivered 1.2% and guidance was cut mid-year from 3-4% to ~2%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is negative and meaningless as a growth proxy: GBP2.6bn of buybacks over five years shrank book value while earnings grew. EPS CAGRs are flattered by the same buybacks and by the FY2020 COVID trough. Neither is used; the forward path is anchored to guidance and the end-market growth estimates (energy ~5%, electrification ~6%, US housing ~5% recovery, aviation ~4%).

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 lands on guidance: ~4% organic (John Crane H2-weighted as Middle East disruption persists through H1; Flex-Tek H1-weighted on Thermal Solutions/DRC and Aerospace, with US construction still subdued), -1% FX, plus the DRC annualisation, for ~5.5% reported. From FY2028 organic growth runs at ~4.5% -- below the 5-7% target, because the only continuing-basis evidence (1.2% in FY2026, a mid-year guidance cut) does not yet earn the algorithm -- fading to 2.5% by year 10. Headline EBITDA margin moves from 23.1% to 25% (HOP ~22%, mid-range) via the Acceleration Plan, aftermarket mix and operating leverage. Capex steps up to ~GBP65m in FY2027 then normalises to the 2-3% guided range. Cash tax 25% throughout. The GBP1.5bn of remaining buybacks is value-neutral (cash in the bridge, count flat). Terminal value at 9% / 2.5% is 15.8x year-10 FCF, just inside the 16x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: Energy-security capex (LNG, where ~90% of the largest facilities use John Crane seals), the US housing recovery from FY2028, record aerospace backlogs, and data-centre cooling demand through DRC/Wattco together deliver the 5-7% organic algorithm from FY2028 for four years, with bolt-on M&A on top not modelled. Margin reaches 26.3% EBITDA (HOP ~23%, top of range) as aftermarket share rises and the Acceleration Plan over-delivers. The asbestos liability is divested, removing the ~GBP20m/yr cash drag (not separately credited here). Terminal growth 3.0%; the 16x cap binds (Gordon would be 17.2x).
scenario_narratives.bear: The Middle East disruption that cost John Crane ~GBP20m in FY2026 persists, energy capex softens into FY2028 as oil prices fall, and US housing starts stay depressed on mortgage rates, so growth drops to 0.5-1% in FY2028-29 before recovering to a 2% trend; the two-segment group proves more cyclical than the old four-segment one. Tariff cost pass-through lags and negative operating leverage pull EBITDA margin to 22% (HOP ~19%) before a partial recovery to 23%; capex is cut to defend cash. Activist pressure forces more buybacks at full prices rather than reinvestment. Asbestos/Titeflex outflows continue at ~GBP20m+/yr and the divestiture process stalls (not deducted, see notes). Terminal growth 2.0%, Gordon 14.6x FCF.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the continuing two-segment Smiths (John Crane + Flex-Tek) on unlevered owner free cash flow built from FY2026 continuing-basis components -- headline EBITDA 23.1%, SBC 1%, D&A 2.5% incl. right-of-use, capex 2% rising to the guided range plus ROU renewal, 25% cash tax, negative working-capital capture -- discounted at a GBP 9% WACC, with the GBP1,747m year-end net cash added once in the bridge and the fully diluted year-end count of 295.6m held flat because SBC is expensed. The pre-divestiture history (FY2019-24) informs margins and cyclicality but is not extrapolated across the FY2025 restatement boundary. Management's 5-7% / 21-23% medium-term algorithm is the bull axis; the base sits below it until the continuing group has shown more than one year of delivery. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and the 25/50/25 weights, not in the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Transformation execution: the continuing group has one year of history (FY2026 organic +1.2%, guidance cut mid-year); the 5-7% organic / 21-23% margin algorithm is unproven at this portfolio shape

End-market concentration: John Crane to oil & gas / energy capex cycles (~58% of revenue) and Flex-Tek Construction (~19%) to US residential construction, which is currently weak with no dated recovery catalyst
Middle East conflict: ~GBP20m FY2026 revenue impact on John Crane; region ~7% of revenue; FY2027 guidance assumes disruption through H1 and recovery in H2

Legacy litigation not deducted: John Crane Inc. asbestos provision GBP153m and Titeflex GBP29m (~62p/share if taken at book, ~GBP20m/yr cash drag); divestiture process announced 22 Sep 2026 but unexecuted and the ten-year forecast horizon understates a liability with claims beyond it

Capital allocation: ~GBP1.5bn of buybacks still to execute through CY2027 at ~29x trailing headline earnings; value-neutral in this model only if executed at or below intrinsic value, and activist pressure (Engine Capital, Elliott) may push for more
FX translation: ~63% of revenue is USD; each USD0.10 move is ~GBP16m of operating profit; FY2027 guidance embeds ~1% headwind
Tariffs: US-UK and US-China tariff volatility already cited as a FY2026 margin pressure; pass-through lag is the bear-case margin axis
Terminal-value weight: ~55-60% of EV sits in the terminal value at a 9% WACC; each 1pp of WACC is worth roughly 12-15% of value
Cyber: FY2025 incident; management rates the likelihood 'almost certain'; FY2027 capex includes GBP25m of security remediation

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (regularMarketPrice, LSE regular close) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2088-2885 GBp.
data_sources.financials: SMIN.L_Annual_FY2026.txt (Annual Report FY2026, year ended 31 July 2026, published 22 Sep 2026): note 1 segment analysis (continuing revenue, HOP, D&A, SBC), note 8 EPS share counts, note 24 share capital and buybacks, note 29 cash-flow, note 30 APMs (headline operating cash-flow 384, headline EBITDA 447, net cash 1,747, free cash-flow 256), note 4 finance income; critical accounting judgements (asbestos provision 153, Titeflex 29). SMIN.L_Presentation_FY2026.txt for FY2027 technical guidance (capex ~65, ETR 24-25%, net finance expense 10-15, FX ~-1%, acquisition revenue contributions). core_metrics / kpis via make dcf-context for the FY2018-FY2026 history; FY2025 and H1 FY2025 restated to continuing basis by the financial-parser agent.
data_sources.qualitative: SMIN.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): business model, moat, competitive position (Frost & Sullivan seal market shares), growth drivers, bull/bear cases, FY2027 guidance and medium-term targets.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026 continuing operations (John Crane 1,130 + Flex-Tek 807), FY2026 AR note 1 segment table. FY2025 continuing restated 1,898 (+2.1% reported, +1.2% organic). Earlier years include Smiths Detection and Smiths Interconnect and are NOT comparable.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 31 July 2026: 295,807,098 issued (note 24) less 1,493,880 held in the Employee Benefit Trust plus 1,307,740 potentially dilutive shares (note 8) = 295.6m. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. NOT the FY2026 weighted-average diluted 314.6m, which is inflated by the timing of the 33.9m shares bought back during the year. 1,561,624 repurchased shares were unsettled at year end (still in issue, GBP41m accrued, cash not yet paid) and the close-period buyback instruction created a further GBP278m liability: neither has yet reduced cash or the count, so year-end cash and year-end shares are on a consistent pre-buyback basis. A further 8.9m shares were repurchased 1 Aug to 22 Sep 2026; value-neutral under the flat-count convention.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company-defined net cash GBP1,747m at 31 July 2026 (note 18 / credit metrics table): cash 2,956 less gross debt 1,204 (borrowings 537 current + 556 non-current, lease liabilities 24 + 80, other ~7). Lease liabilities are INSIDE gross debt, consistent with lease treatment (A). Excludes the GBP319m accrued buyback liabilities (see share_count_basis) and the GBP153m asbestos / GBP29m Titeflex litigation provisions (see notes).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Continuing-operations, unlevered: headline operating cash-flow GBP384m (FY2026 AR note 30; 96% conversion of HOP 399; after capex 39 and working capital, BEFORE interest, tax and lease repayments) less headline tax charge GBP89m (24.4%) = 295. The company's own statutory free cash-flow of GBP256m is total group, includes Detection for 11 months and Interconnect for 8, and is depressed by GBP131m of disposal transaction/separation costs, so it is not a usable base. last_fcf = 295 - SBC 19 - interest income 0 = 276. Under lease treatment (A) the engine also charges ~GBP23m/yr of right-of-use renewal through the capex path, so the engine's year-1 owner FCF sits ~GBP20-25m below this anchor on a like-for-like basis.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR note 1 segment analysis: share-based payment John Crane 3 + Flex-Tek 2 + corporate 14 = GBP19m continuing (FY2025 restated: 15). Total-group figures are GBP24m (cash-flow add-back, note 29) and GBP26m (equity statement). No cash taxes on net-share settlement are disclosed (kpis EquityAwardTaxes = 0); the GBP43m 'share award settlement' is EBT share purchases, i.e. the buyback-like mechanism that keeps the count flat, not an additional cost.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income was GBP44m (note 4), but reported_fcf is built from headline operating cash-flow, which by the company's APM definition excludes interest received and paid. Nothing to strip; the GBP2,956m cash is added once, in the bridge. FY2027 net finance expense guided GBP10-15m.
inputs.buyback_note: GBP839m cash in FY2026 for 33,877,205 shares cancelled (note 24). GBP1.5bn of the GBP3bn disposal-linked return programme completed; a further ~GBP1.5bn to run through CY2027. Value-neutral in this model: cash stays in the bridge and the count stays flat.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP (pounds, millions); LSE quote in GBp (pence). fx_rate 100 = pence per pound, a fixed definitional ratio with no date or source dependency. Per-share values are computed in GBP and multiplied by 100 to the quote currency. No dual listing needed for parity.
inputs.price_note: Regular LSE close (16:15 UTC); not an after-hours print. 52-week range 2088-2885.
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP-denominated flows discounted at a GBP-built rate: 10y gilt ~4.5% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.0 = cost of equity ~9.5%; EUR1.3bn of bonds (~13% of EV at ~3% after tax) pull the blend to ~8.7%. Rounded to 9.0% and applied to all three scenarios: cyclicality (energy capex, US housing), Middle East disruption and transformation-execution risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate. ~63% of revenue is USD, but the flows are reported and valued in GBP.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. Lease liabilities GBP104m (24 current + 80 non-current) sit inside gross debt 1,204 and therefore inside the GBP1,747m net cash. Lease principal (GBP41m total group; ~GBP25m continuing) is NOT deducted from the flows and lease interest (GBP6m) is a financing cost. Ongoing right-of-use asset renewal is charged through the capex path at ~1.2% of revenue (FY2026 continuing ROU depreciation 23 / 1,937), and the D&A path (2.5% FY2026 = PPE dep 22 + ROU dep 23 + software amort 3) includes ROU depreciation. Amortisation of acquired intangibles (GBP33m) is excluded from headline EBITDA and from D&A, consistently.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest GBP2m profit share, immaterial; no adjustment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company; industrial engineering, cyclical, non-US filer -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. BASIS: FY2026 continuing operations (John Crane + Flex-Tek) after the FY2026 disposals of Smiths Interconnect (Molex, GBP1.3bn EV, 31 Mar 2026) and Smiths Detection (CVC, GBP2.0bn EV, 30 Jun 2026). All driver anchors are continuing-basis: revenue 1,937, headline EBITDA 447 (23.1%), HOP 399 (20.6%), capex 39 (2.0%, guided ~65 in FY2027 including a GBP25m security step-up; medium term 2-3%), continuing SBC 19, headline ETR 24.4% (guided 24-25%). The FY2026 statutory PAT of GBP1,972m includes a GBP1,690m disposal gain and is not an earnings base; continuing statutory net income GBP155m is after GBP33m acquired-intangible amortisation, a GBP57m pension settlement loss and GBP27m restructuring. The FY2024->FY2025 revenue 'decline' in the history is the divestiture restatement, not operating deterioration. WORKING CAPITAL: continuing FY2026 absorbed ~GBP24m (EBITDA 447 - capex 39 - headline operating cash 384); manufacturer with receivables + inventory > payables, so wc_capture is NEGATIVE (-15% of the revenue change). CONTINGENT LIABILITIES NOT DEDUCTED: John Crane Inc. asbestos provision GBP153m (FY2025: 191m; ten-year Bates White forecast; ~GBP20m/yr cash outflow over five years per CFO) and Titeflex CSST provision GBP29m. Per the orchestrator's instruction these are carried as a qualitative risk and in the bear weight rather than as a hard bridge deduction; for the record, deducting both at book would be ~GBP182m = ~62p/share (~2-3% of base IV). Management launched a process on 22 Sep 2026 to divest the asbestos liability, which would crystallise roughly that amount in cash. Also not deducted: the GBP319m accrued buyback liabilities (value-neutral at market). Non-headline cash items (restructuring 27, pension settlement, disposal costs) are treated as transformation one-offs that do not recur in the continuing run-rate.

bear.narrative: FY2026's 1.2% turns out to be the run-rate, not the trough.

base.growth_note: FY2027: ~4% organic guidance -1% FX headwind +~3.7% DRC Heat Transfer annualisation (GBP35.5m in 4 months of FY2026 -> ~GBP106m full year) -~1.3% Flex-Tek general-industrial disposals = ~5.5% reported. Then 4.5% organic (below the 5-7% target; FY2026 was 1.2%) fading to 2.5% terminal.
base.margin_note: FY2026 headline EBITDA 23.1% (HOP 20.6%). FY2027 HOP guided ~21% -> EBITDA ~23.5%. Matures to 25.0% EBITDA = ~22% HOP after D&A rises to 3.0%, the middle of the 21-23% medium-term range; Acceleration Plan GBP30-35m by FY2027 and aftermarket mix.
base.capex_note: Cash capex + right-of-use renewal (lease treatment A). FY2027: guided ~GBP65m (3.2%, includes GBP25m security systems) + 1.2% ROU = 4.4%. Medium term: 2-3% guided cash capex (use 2.4-2.5%) + 1.2% ROU = ~3.6-3.7%.
base.narrative: Smiths delivers a credible but not heroic version of the new algorithm.

bull.narrative: The 5-7% organic algorithm is hit from FY2028 and margins reach the top of 21-23%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the 'new Smiths' has one year of continuing-basis history and it missed (1.2% organic vs 3-4% initial guidance), management's own principal-risk register rates failure to deliver post-transformation growth as very-high gross risk, and the group is now concentrated in two cyclical end-markets (energy capex, US housing) with a live Middle East drag; there is no solvency or refinancing risk (GBP1.75bn net cash), which is why bear is not higher. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once -- housing recovery, sustained energy capex, data-centre M&A integration, and margin at the top of the range -- and the bull case is roughly what the current share price already discounts.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
